draft.title: Other ways to invest
card: An owner who puts money into a business could have invested it elsewhere. Common choices are a bank account, shares or property.
savings in a bank earn interest. The return is usually low, but the risk is usually low too.
shares are part ownership of a company. Property is land or buildings. Both can earn income and rise in value, but they can also fall in value.
A business carries risk, so the owner should expect to earn more from it than from these other choices. If it earns the same or less, the risk is not worth taking.
draft.remember: A business must earn more than the owner's other options to be worth its risk.

a.q: Dev has $50 000 to invest. He could leave it in a bank account or put it into his own café. Why should the café aim to earn more than the bank would pay?
opts: The café has more risk than the bank account
The café needs more money than the bank account
The bank account earns no return at all
The bank account has more risk than the café
a.why: A café can lose money, while a bank account is usually safe. The owner takes on extra risk, so the café should earn more than the bank to be worth it. The bank does pay interest, so the bank earning nothing is wrong.
a.clue: Think about which choice could lose Dev's money.

b.q: Priya earns 6% a year from shares. She is thinking of putting the same money into her own bakery. The bakery would earn 4% a year. What should she conclude?
opts: The bakery is not worth the risk compared with shares
The bakery is worth it because it is her own business
The bakery is worth it because it earns some return
The bakery is not worth it because shares carry no risk
b.why: The bakery earns less than shares, and it also carries business risk. So it is not worth the risk on money alone. Shares do carry risk, so the last option is wrong, and earning some return is not enough.
b.clue: Compare the two returns first, then think about risk.

a.best: The café has more risk than the bank account

b.best: The bakery is not worth the risk compared with shares

problems.detail: The why for (b) calls the 'shares carry no risk' option 'the last option', but options are shown in random order. In this order it is the second option, so the explanation would confuse students.
